headline: Contact re-established — an easy Copenhagen run breaks the week-long gap. It sat controlled and short, exactly what a restart should be. Strength and a fresh threshold read remain the untouched gaps.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The run drought finally ended with a short, low-effort outing that stayed entirely in easy zones — a sensible re-entry rather than a statement. That single session doesn't change the fact that the recent four-week block was dominated by one enormous trail effort, and the picture now is a base that's fully intact but a cadence that's still only one session deep. Strength remains the persistently quiet corner, with almost nothing in the last month and no current streak to build from. Steps stay high and remarkably flat between training and rest days, so background activity is carrying real daily load even when structured sessions are sparse. Load and recovery streams remain too thin to lean on. The honest read: the base is durable, the restart has begun, but rhythm across both running and strength still has to be rebuilt from this point.
sections.trends: Zoom out and the year-to-date shape is strongly positive — cumulative distance sits far ahead of the same point last year, which tells you the annual trajectory is genuinely building rather than merely holding. The recent weeks, though, are lumpy: a massive Åre spike followed by a near-empty stretch, which reads as cyclical-to-irregular at the short horizon even while the long horizon climbs. That's consistent with the athlete's year-round, non-periodised approach, but the last month leaned heavily on a single big block rather than distributed consistency. The shape makes sense given the goals; the open question is whether the next stretch spreads load more evenly.
sections.threshold: The threshold reading is now two months old and unchanged, because nothing since has been the kind of sustained tempo that would refresh it. The two late-August runs touched Z3–Z4 and held respectable pace, which is directionally reassuring that top-end aerobic capacity hasn't gone anywhere. But there's a genuine gap between demonstrated durability and a current, verified threshold number — the stale reading is a measurement gap, not evidence of decline. Until a clean sustained effort lands, treat threshold fitness as intact-but-unconfirmed.
sections.zones: Today's run sat cleanly in easy territory with a controlled ceiling — appropriate for a first run back after a week off, and no reason to force intensity into it. Looking across recent sessions, the distribution is polarised in a way that fits the athlete: enormous Z1 volume from the trail block, two genuinely mixed runs with real Z3–Z4 time, and little in between. That's a reasonable shape, but the persistent absence is the sustained threshold middle — the one session type that's been missing for weeks and would round out the block's intent.
sections.hr_comparison: Strength HR history shows the familiar pattern — mostly low-zone with occasional pushes into Z2–Z3 depending on the session's circuit density — but there's simply no recent strength work to comment on, so nothing new here. Today's run carried clean HR and its average and ceiling agree with an easy effort, no dropout to flag. Nothing notable in sensor-source agreement this cycle.
sections.calendar: The calendar tells the real story: a dense trail cluster in mid-August, then a stark blank, then two isolated late-August runs, then a week of silence broken today. That's not a consistency problem in the long-streak sense — the weekly running streak is remarkably long — but it is a rhythm problem at the day-to-day level, where sessions have been arriving in bursts and gaps rather than a steady weekly cadence. The value now is in stacking a second and third run close behind this one so the restart becomes a pattern rather than another isolated touch.
sections.personal_bests: The short-distance PBs date from last autumn and none are within reach off a single easy run — that's a speed-sharpening question that only becomes live once regular running and some threshold work are back in place. The ultra durability is clearly current given the Åre block, but that's a different quality than the 5K–Half bests. Nothing actionable on PBs today; the focus is rebuilding cadence first.

watch_items: Watch whether a second and third run land close behind today's — that's what turns this restart from a touch into a rhythm.
Watch whether strength reappears in any form, since it still has no recent anchor and the streak sits at zero.
Watch whether a sustained tempo finally shows up to refresh the two-month-old threshold read.
Watch whether the coming stretch distributes load across the week rather than clustering into bursts and gaps.
